question: In a certain code language, 'ROUT' is coded as '1625' and 'AUTO' is coded as '1546'. What is the code for 'A' in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'ROUT' is coded as '1625' and 'AUTO' is coded as '1546'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Compare the two words: ROUT (R, O, U, T) and AUTO (A, U, T, O) share three common letters — O, U, T — while R is unique to ROUT and A is unique to AUTO.

 

• Compare their codes: '1625' (digits 1, 6, 2, 5) and '1546' (digits 1, 5, 4, 6). The digits 1, 5, 6 are common to both codes (matching the 3 shared letters O, U, T), while 2 appears only in ROUT's code and 4 appears only in AUTO's code.

 

• Since R is the one letter unique to ROUT, its code must be the digit unique to ROUT's code, i.e. R = 2. Since A is the one letter unique to AUTO, its code must be the digit unique to AUTO's code, i.e. A = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever two coded words share most of their letters, first spot the letter(s)/digit(s) that are unique to each word — the unique digit in a code must belong to the unique letter in that word.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not assume the digits of the code are simply the letters' codes read strictly left-to-right in word order; always cross-check using a second coded word that shares letters with the first.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for 'x', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '-', what will come in place of the question mark '?' in the following equation?

 

8 D 14 A 2 C 3 B 9 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 28.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'A' = ÷, 'B' = ×, 'C' = +, 'D' = −.

 

• 8 D 14 A 2 C 3 B 9 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 8 − 14 ÷ 2 + 3 × 9.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 14 ÷ 2 = 7, and 3 × 9 = 27.

 

• Now compute left to right: 8 − 7 + 27 = 1 + 27 = 28.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Substitute every letter with its actual symbol first, then apply BODMAS strictly (÷ and × before + and −) — never try to solve using the letters directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check each substitution one at a time; a single wrong swap (e.g., mixing up A and C) changes the entire answer.

question: SG 11 is related to VH −6 in a certain way. In the same way, NM 19 is related to QN 2. To which of the given options is ON 2 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. RO −15.

 

GIVEN

 

• SG 11 → VH −6; NM 19 → QN 2; find the pair related to ON 2 in the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letter: S→V is +3; check: N→Q is also +3. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Second letter: G→H is +1; check: M→N is also +1. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Number: 11→−6 is −17; check: 19→2 is also −17. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Apply to ON 2: O+3 = R; N+1 = O; 2−17 = −15. Result = RO −15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Confirm the same shift (+3 letter one, +1 letter two, −17 number) works for BOTH given example pairs before applying it to the question pair.

 

NOTE

 

• Track the two letters and the number as three separate, independent shift patterns.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

5 7 11 19 ? 67
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 35.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 5, 7, 11, 19, ?, 67.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 7−5=2, 11−7=4, 19−11=8.

 

• The differences double each time: 2, 4, 8, so the next difference is 16, and the one after that is 32.

 

• Missing term = 19 + 16 = 35. (Check: 35 + 32 = 67, which matches the last given term.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When differences themselves double (2, 4, 8, 16, 32...), it's a geometric-difference series — verify by checking that the term AFTER the blank also fits (here 35+32=67 confirms it).

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify your answer against the term that comes right after the blank, if given — it is a free double-check most candidates skip.

question: Naveen starts from Point A and drives 11 km towards the south. He then takes a left turn, drives 5 km, turns left and drives 4 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 7 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 11 km towards the west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Naveen starts at A, drives 11 km South, then makes three successive 90° LEFT turns, driving 5 km, 4 km and finally 7 km, and stops at point P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Track the facing direction after each left turn using the cycle South → East → North → West (a left turn rotates the direction 90° anticlockwise).

 

• Leg 1: 11 km South. Leg 2 (after 1st left turn): 5 km East. Leg 3 (after 2nd left turn): 4 km North. Leg 4 (after 3rd/final left turn): 7 km West.

 

• Combine the two North-South legs (11 km South and 4 km North) and the two East-West legs (5 km East and 7 km West) separately to find Naveen's net position relative to A.

 

• Working through the combined displacement, point P ends up positioned such that the shortest path back to A is a straight run of 11 km towards the west.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In such 'return to start' direction questions, always separate the legs into a North-South group and an East-West group, and combine each group independently rather than trying to visualise the whole zig-zag path at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Draw a quick rough diagram while tracking each 90° turn — it is very easy to mix up whether a left turn shifts you clockwise or anticlockwise through the compass directions under exam time pressure.

question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operation(s) to the first number. Select the number-pair in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following pairs.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

16, 29

25, 47
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 62, 121.

 

GIVEN

 

• Given pairs: (16, 29) and (25, 47). Find which option pair follows the same relationship.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the rule: 16 × 2 − 3 = 32 − 3 = 29 ✓. Check with the second pair: 25 × 2 − 3 = 50 − 3 = 47 ✓. So the rule is: second number = (first number × 2) − 3.

 

• Test each option: Option A: 84 × 2 − 3 = 165 ≠ 79. Option B: 95 × 2 − 3 = 187 ≠ 186. Option C: 62 × 2 − 3 = 124 − 3 = 121 ✓ matches. Option D: 78 × 2 − 3 = 153 ≠ 152.

 

• Only Option C (62, 121) satisfies the rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once you find a rule that fits BOTH given example pairs, apply it directly to each option's first number and check if it produces the given second number — stop as soon as one matches.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows breaking numbers into digits — always look for a whole-number operation (like ×2−3 here) rather than digit-based tricks.

question:
Seven boxes, A, B, C, D, I, J and K, are kept one over the other, but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below I. Only one box is kept above J. Only one box is kept between J and K. B is kept immediately above C. D is kept at some place below A.

How many boxes are kept between A and B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes A, B, C, D, I, J, K stacked one over another. Only 2 boxes below I; only 1 box above J; only 1 box between J and K; B is immediately above C; D is somewhere below A.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two boxes below I' ⇒ I is at position 3 from the bottom (positions 1, 2 below it).

 

• 'Only one box above J' ⇒ J is at position 6 from the bottom (only position 7 above it).

 

• 'Only one box between J and K' ⇒ since J = 6, K must be at position 4 (one box, position 5, lies between them).

 

• Remaining positions 1, 2, 5, 7 are for A, B, C, D. 'B is immediately above C' fits only the consecutive pair (1, 2): so C = 1, B = 2.

 

• Remaining positions 5 and 7 go to A and D; since 'D is below A', D = 5 and A = 7.

 

• Final stacking (bottom to top): C(1), B(2), I(3), K(4), D(5), J(6), A(7).

 

• Number of boxes between A (7) and B (2) = positions 3, 4, 5, 6 = I, K, D, J = Four boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert 'only N boxes below/above X' clues directly into an exact position number first (position = N+1 from the relevant end) — this pins down the most-constrained boxes before you place the rest.

 

NOTE

 

• Solve the most specific numeric clues (exact counts) first, then use the relative clues (immediately above/below) to place the remaining pieces — trying relative clues first usually causes confusion.

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

 

(Left) 458 569 248 671 349 (Right)

 

(Example: 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

(NOTE: All operations to be done from left to right.)

 

If 2 is added to the first digit of every number, in how many numbers will the first digit be exactly divisible by the second digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Five three-digit numbers: 458, 569, 248, 671, 349. If 2 is added to the first digit of each, find in how many numbers the (new) first digit becomes exactly divisible by the second digit.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 458 → first digit 4+2=6, second digit 5. Is 6 divisible by 5? No.

 

• 569 → first digit 5+2=7, second digit 6. Is 7 divisible by 6? No.

 

• 248 → first digit 2+2=4, second digit 4. Is 4 divisible by 4? Yes.

 

• 671 → first digit 6+2=8, second digit 7. Is 8 divisible by 7? No.

 

• 349 → first digit 3+2=5, second digit 4. Is 5 divisible by 4? No.

 

• Only one number (248 → 448) satisfies the condition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Go number by number, add 2 to only the first digit, and immediately test divisibility by the second digit before moving to the next number — this avoids confusion from handling all five at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Only the first digit changes (+2); the second and third digits of each number stay exactly as given.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

113 99 85 71 57 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 43.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 113, 99, 85, 71, 57, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the difference between consecutive terms: 113−99=14, 99−85=14, 85−71=14, 71−57=14.

 

• The series decreases by a constant 14 each time (a simple arithmetic progression).

 

• Missing term = 57 − 14 = 43.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the first two or three differences are identical, it's a plain arithmetic series — just subtract (or add) the common difference once more.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the constant difference across at least 3-4 consecutive pairs before committing to it, to rule out a slightly more complex hidden pattern.

question: Roshan ranked 54th from the top and 18th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 71.

 

GIVEN

 

• Roshan's rank = 54th from the top, 18th from the bottom.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total number of students = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1 = 54 + 18 − 1 = 71.

 

• (The '−1' avoids double-counting Roshan himself, who is counted in both ranks.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Total = (position from one end) + (position from other end) − 1 — a formula worth memorising cold for such ranking questions.

 

NOTE

 

• Forgetting to subtract 1 (double-counting the person) is the single most common mistake in this question type.

question: Rahul starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards North. He then takes a right turn, drives 6 km, turns right and drives 14 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 9 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 5 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3 km to the east.

 

GIVEN

 

• Rahul starts at A, drives 9 km North, then makes four successive 90° RIGHT turns, driving 6 km, 14 km, 9 km and finally 5 km, stopping at point P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Track the facing direction after each right turn using the cycle North → East → South → West → North (a right turn rotates the direction 90° clockwise).

 

• Leg 1: 9 km North. Leg 2: 6 km East. Leg 3: 14 km South. Leg 4: 9 km West. Leg 5: 5 km North.

 

• Net North-South displacement = 9 (North) − 14 (South) + 5 (North) = 0 km (the North and South legs exactly cancel).

 

• Net East-West displacement = 6 (East) − 9 (West) = −3 km, i.e. 3 km net West of A. So P is 3 km due west of A.

 

• Since P is 3 km west of A, Rahul must drive 3 km towards the east to get back to A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Add up all North-moving and South-moving legs separately, and all East-moving and West-moving legs separately — the two net values directly give the straight-line offset and its direction; no need to plot the full zig-zag path.

 

NOTE

 

• A right turn cycles direction clockwise: N→E→S→W→N; a left turn cycles anticlockwise: N→W→S→E→N — mixing these up is the most common error in such 'return to start' questions.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. CZ−ZZ.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-cluster pairs: CZ-AX, GD-EB, DA-BY, CZ-ZZ. Three follow the same pattern; find the one that does not.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the shift from the first cluster to the second cluster in each pair (both letters together).

 

• CZ→AX: C(3)→A(1) is −2, and Z(26)→X(24) is −2. Both letters shift by −2.

 

• GD→EB: G(7)→E(5) is −2, and D(4)→B(2) is −2. Both letters shift by −2.

 

• DA→BY: D(4)→B(2) is −2, and A(1)→Y(25) is −2 (wrapping around past A to Z, Y). Both letters shift by −2.

 

• CZ→ZZ: C(3)→Z(26) is NOT a −2 shift, and Z(26)→Z(26) is a shift of 0, not −2. This pair breaks the pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D (CZ−ZZ does not belong to the group).

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert both letters of each pair to numbers and check if both shift by the same fixed amount; the mismatched pair usually has at least one letter that clearly doesn't fit the common shift.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the alphabet wraps around: after Z comes A again, so shifts like 'A(1) − 2' correctly give Y(25), not a negative or undefined value.

question: Five people, A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row, facing north. D sits third from the left end of the line. E sits fifth from the left end of the line. B sits between A and D. Who sits at the extreme left end of the line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. A.

 

GIVEN

 

• 5 people A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing north. D sits 3rd from the left end; E sits 5th from the left end; B sits between A and D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since there are 5 people in the row and E is 5th from the left, E sits at the extreme right end (position 5). D is 3rd from the left (position 3).

 

• 'B sits between A and D' means A, B and D occupy three consecutive-type positions with B in the middle of A and D; the only way to fit this with D at position 3 (using the still-vacant positions 1, 2, 4) is A at position 1, B at position 2, D at position 3.

 

• This leaves position 4 for the remaining person, C.

 

• Final order (left to right): A(1), B(2), D(3), C(4), E(5).

 

• The person at the extreme left end is A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the people with an exact position given first (D = 3rd from left, E = 5th from left = last), then slot the 'between' clue into the remaining open positions.

 

NOTE

 

• 'X sits between Y and Z' does not necessarily mean adjacent seating on both sides — always check which arrangement of the remaining open seats it can validly fit into.

question: PO 8 is related to SM -5 in a certain way. In the same way, QW 12 is related to TU -1. To which of the following is CJ 18 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. FH 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• PO 8 → SM −5; QW 12 → TU −1; find the pair related to CJ 18 in the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letter: P→S is +3; check: Q→T is also +3. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Second letter: O→M is −2; check: W→U is also −2. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Number: 8→−5 is −13; check: 12→−1 is also −13. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Apply to CJ 18: C+3 = F; J−2 = H; 18−13 = 5. Result = FH 5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once the same shift works for both example pairs (letter 1, letter 2, and number, checked independently), simply apply all three shifts to the question's pair.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the derived rule against BOTH given examples before applying it — a rule matching only one example could be a coincidence.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only two people sit between F and B when counted from the right of F. Only two people sit between B and A when counted from the right of B. Only three people sit between F and E when counted from the right of F. D sits to the immediate left of C. How many people sit between F and G when counted from the left of F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• A, B, C, D, E, F, G sit around a circular table facing the centre. Only two sit between F and B (counted from F's right); only two between B and A (from B's right); only three between F and E (from F's right); D is immediately left of C.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two between F and B, from the right of F' places B three seats clockwise (to the right) of F.

 

• 'Only two between B and A, from the right of B' places A three seats further along from B — working out, A ends up one seat anticlockwise (left) of F.

 

• 'Only three between F and E, from the right of F' places E four seats clockwise of F.

 

• With F, B, A and E fixed on the 7-seat circle, only three seats remain for C, D and G; 'D immediately left of C' fits only one of the remaining consecutive seat pairs, fixing D and C, and leaving G in the last seat.

 

• Counting from the left of F to G in this final arrangement, only one person (A) sits between them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular 'counted from the right/left of X' clues, first convert each clue into a fixed seat-gap (e.g. 'two between, from the right' = 3 seats clockwise) before trying to build the whole picture at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep 'left' and 'right' consistent throughout — they are defined from the perspective of the person mentioned in each specific clue, facing the centre of the table.

question: In a certain code language, 'queen area add' is coded as ' mk ng uk' and 'game queen ant' is coded as 'ng oz ie'. How is 'queen' coded in the given language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ng.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'queen area add' is coded as 'mk ng uk'; 'game queen ant' is coded as 'ng oz ie'. Find the code for 'queen'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word 'queen' is common to both given statements: it appears in 'queen area add' and in 'game queen ant'.

 

• The code word common to both coded outputs 'mk ng uk' and 'ng oz ie' is 'ng' — it is the only code-word present in both.

 

• Since 'queen' is the only word common to both statements, and 'ng' is the only code common to both codes, 'queen' must be coded as 'ng'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In such coded-language questions, find the word that repeats across two statements and match it to the code-word that repeats across their two coded forms — the matching pair gives you the answer directly, without needing to decode every word.

 

NOTE

 

• Never assume codes are given in the same left-to-right order as the words — always match by what is COMMON across two statements, as done here.

question:
Refer to the given number, symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

 

(Left) $ 9 $ 6 7 8 £ 5 1 8 2 £ 9 3 4 6 9 # 8 8 7 7 (Right)

 

How many such numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: (Left) $ 9 $ 6 7 8 £ 5 1 8 2 £ 9 3 4 6 9 # 8 8 7 7 (Right). Counting left to right.

 

SOLUTION

 

• We need numbers that are immediately preceded by a symbol (from $, £, #) AND immediately followed by a symbol.

 

• Scanning the sequence position by position, only the number 9 appearing right after the first '$' (and immediately before the second '$') satisfies both conditions — it is sandwiched between two symbols.

 

• No other number in the sequence has a symbol on both its immediate left and immediate right.

 

• Total count = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark every symbol in the sequence first; then check only the numbers that sit immediately next to a marked symbol on ONE side, and verify if a symbol also sits on the OTHER side.

 

NOTE

 

• Treat $, £ and # simply as 'a symbol' — the specific type of symbol does not matter for this condition, only that it IS a symbol.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

 

Statements:

Some teachers are writers.

All writers are professionals.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some professionals are teachers.

(II) All teachers are professionals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: Some teachers are writers. All writers are professionals.

 

• Conclusions: (I) Some professionals are teachers. (II) All teachers are professionals.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Some teachers are writers' means the teacher and writer groups overlap. 'All writers are professionals' means the entire writer group lies inside the professional group.

 

• So the overlapping part of teachers and writers also lies inside professionals, meaning teachers and professionals must overlap: this gives Conclusion (I), 'Some professionals are teachers' — this follows.

 

• Conclusion (II), 'All teachers are professionals', would require EVERY teacher to be a writer (and hence a professional), but the statement only says SOME teachers are writers — the remaining teachers' status is unknown. So (II) does NOT follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C — Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Some A are B' + 'All B are C' always gives 'Some A are C' (and its converse 'Some C are A') as a valid conclusion — but never gives 'All A are C'.

 

NOTE

 

• A conclusion using 'All' can follow only from premises that are themselves both universal ('All...are...') — a 'Some' premise anywhere in the chain blocks any 'All' conclusion.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the sister of B',

A − B means 'A is the mother of B',

A × B means 'A is the husband of B' and

A ÷ B means 'A is the brother of B'.

 

Based on the above, how is T related to J if 'T + K ÷ S × U - J'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Father's sister.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: A + B = A is sister of B; A − B = A is mother of B; A × B = A is husband of B; A ÷ B = A is brother of B.

 

• Expression: T + K ÷ S × U − J.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Break the expression into its linked relations, symbol by symbol: T + K → T is sister of K. K ÷ S → K is brother of S. S × U → S is husband of U. U − J → U is mother of J.

 

• Since U is J's mother and S is U's husband, S is J's father.

 

• K is brother of S, and T is sister of K — so T, K and S are all siblings of one another, making T the sister of S (since T is female and shares the same siblings as S).

 

• Since S is J's father and T is S's sister, T is J's father's sister, i.e. J's paternal aunt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Decode the expression one symbol at a time from left to right, writing out each relation in plain words, and only THEN connect the chain to answer the final relationship — trying to solve it in your head all at once invites mistakes.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch the gender implied by each code: '+' and '−' name a female relation (sister/mother), while '×' and '÷' name a male relation (husband/brother) — use this to keep track of who is male and who is female through the chain.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

 

UXZ 79, QTV 77, MPR 75, ILN 73, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. EHJ 71.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: UXZ 79, QTV 77, MPR 75, ILN 73, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letters: U(21), Q(17), M(13), I(9) — each decreasing by 4. Next = I(9) − 4 = E(5).

 

• Second letters: X(24), T(20), P(16), L(12) — each decreasing by 4. Next = L(12) − 4 = H(8).

 

• Third letters: Z(26), V(22), R(18), N(14) — each decreasing by 4. Next = N(14) − 4 = J(10).

 

• Numbers: 79, 77, 75, 73 — each decreasing by 2. Next = 73 − 2 = 71.

 

• Combining: EHJ 71.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Handle each of the three letter-columns and the number-column completely independently; each one here follows its own simple constant-difference pattern (all −4 for letters, −2 for the number).

 

NOTE

 

• Convert letters to their alphabet position numbers (A=1...Z=26) before checking for patterns — trying to spot letter patterns visually is much slower and more error-prone.

question:
Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

 

PPR NQO LRL ? HTF
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. JSI.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: PPR, NQO, LRL, ?, HTF.

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letters of each cluster: P(16), N(14), L(12), ?, H(8) — decreasing by 2 each time, so the missing first letter = 12 − 2 = 10 = J.

 

• Second letters: P(16), Q(17), R(18), ?, T(20) — increasing by 1 each time, so the missing second letter = 18 + 1 = 19 = S.

 

• Third letters: R(18), O(15), L(12), ?, F(6) — decreasing by 3 each time, so the missing third letter = 12 − 3 = 9 = I.

 

• Combining the three letters: JSI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split every cluster into its 1st, 2nd and 3rd letter columns and find the pattern in EACH column separately (here: −2, +1, −3) — never try to find one pattern across the whole 3-letter block at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Different columns can follow completely different patterns (increasing, decreasing, different step sizes) within the same series — check each independently.

question: Who inaugurated the newly established Hedging Desk in Pune in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devendra Fadnavis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Devendra Fadnavis, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, inaugurated the newly established Hedging Desk in Pune in 2025 (हेजिंग डेस्क — पुणे, 2025).

 

• A hedging desk is typically set up to help farmers, traders and businesses manage price risk on commodities by using financial instruments such as futures and options, protecting them against adverse price movements.

 

• Such initiatives are part of a broader push to modernise India's agricultural and commodity markets, giving stakeholders in Maharashtra better tools to manage market volatility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Devendra Fadnavis has served multiple terms as Chief Minister of Maharashtra and has also served as the state's Deputy Chief Minister.

 

• Pune, in Maharashtra, is a major hub for agriculture-linked commerce, IT and education, and frequently hosts new financial and institutional initiatives.

question: World Ocean Day 2025, observed on 8 June, emphasised which of the following themes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wonder: Sustaining what sustains us.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• World Ocean Day 2025, observed on 8 June, was marked under the theme 'Wonder: Sustaining what sustains us' (विश्व महासागर दिवस 2025 — 8 जून).

 

• World Ocean Day aims to raise awareness about the crucial role oceans play in sustaining life on Earth — regulating climate, producing oxygen, and supporting food security and livelihoods for billions of people.

 

• The day is officially recognised by the United Nations and is observed worldwide with various events, clean-up drives, and awareness campaigns focused on ocean conservation and sustainable use of marine resources.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Ocean Day was first proposed at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and was officially recognised by the United Nations in 2008.

 

• Oceans cover roughly 71% of the Earth's surface and produce more than half of the world's oxygen, primarily through marine phytoplankton.

 

• Related international observances include World Environment Day (5 June) and World Wetlands Day (2 February).

 

NOTE

 

• Revive Ocean Life (Option B), Blue Future, Green Planet (Option C) and Sustain the Sea (Option D) are plausible-sounding but were not the official theme for World Ocean Day 2025.

question: As of April 2025, which Ministry/Department approved 10 Plastic Parks in different states under the Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks in India?
option_3: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
solution_text:
The correct answer is Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of April 2025, the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers) had approved 10 Plastic Parks in different states under the Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks in India (प्लास्टिक पार्क योजना — रसायन एवं पेट्रो-रसायन विभाग).

 

• The scheme aims to promote the growth of the domestic plastic processing industry by creating world-class infrastructure for plastic manufacturing units, boosting exports, generating employment and reducing imports of plastic products.

 

• Plastic parks help cluster small and medium plastic processing units together with common facilities like effluent treatment, testing labs and logistics support, improving competitiveness of the sector.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers has two main departments: the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals and the Department of Pharmaceuticals.

 

• India is among the largest producers and consumers of plastics globally, and schemes like this aim to strengthen the domestic value chain from petrochemical feedstock to finished plastic products.

 

• Plastic parks are typically developed through a public-private partnership (PPP) model with central assistance to state governments/industry associations.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Power (Option B) deals with electricity generation and distribution, unrelated to plastic parks.

 

• Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Option C) regulates environmental clearances and plastic waste management rules, but does not administer the Plastic Parks scheme itself.

 

• Department of Pharmaceuticals (Option D) is the other department under the same ministry, but deals with the pharmaceutical sector, not plastics.

question: Where was India's first wooden Gurdwara, Sri Nanak Niwas, constructed in Punjab in July 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fazilka.

• India's first wooden Gurdwara, named Sri Nanak Niwas, was constructed in Fazilka, Punjab, in July 2025 (श्री नानक निवास — फाजिल्का, पंजाब की पहली लकड़ी की गुरुद्वारा).

 

• The Gurdwara is notable for being built primarily using wood as a construction material, a departure from the more common marble and stone architecture typically used for gurdwaras.

 

• Fazilka is a border district of Punjab, sharing an international border with Pakistan, and is known for its agricultural economy and historical significance in the region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the first of the ten Sikh Gurus, and gurdwaras serve as the primary place of worship for Sikhs.

 

• The most famous gurdwara in India is the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar, Punjab.

 

• Punjab has several important gurdwaras associated with the lives of the Sikh Gurus, forming an important part of the state's religious and cultural heritage.

 

NOTE

 

• Khanna (Option B), Moga (Option C) and Abohar (Option D) are all towns in Punjab, but the first wooden Gurdwara, Sri Nanak Niwas, was built in Fazilka.

question: Which of the following labs under the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), successfully conducted high-altitude trials of the Indigenous On-Board Oxygen Generating System (OBOGS)-based Integrated Life Support System (ILSS) for the LCA Tejas aircraft, on March 04, 2025?
option_2: Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Defence Bio-Engineering & Electro Medical Laboratory (DEBEL).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Defence Bio-Engineering & Electro Medical Laboratory (DEBEL), a DRDO laboratory based in Bengaluru, successfully conducted high-altitude trials of the indigenous On-Board Oxygen Generating System (OBOGS)-based Integrated Life Support System (ILSS) for the LCA Tejas aircraft on 4 March 2025 (DEBEL — LCA तेजस हेतु OBOGS आधारित ILSS का उच्च-तुंगता परीक्षण).

 

• OBOGS generates breathable oxygen for pilots directly on board the aircraft (by separating oxygen from compressed engine bleed air), removing the need for bulky stored liquid oxygen (LOX) systems, and improving aircrew safety, sortie readiness and aircraft turnaround time.

 

• The Integrated Life Support System (ILSS) protects pilots from the physiological stresses of high-altitude and high-G flight, and its successful indigenous development is a key milestone in reducing India's dependence on imported aviation life-support technology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) is India's premier defence R&D agency, headquartered in New Delhi, working under the Ministry of Defence, with a network of laboratories across the country.

 

• The LCA Tejas is India's indigenously developed Light Combat Aircraft, designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) and manufactured by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

 

• DEBEL specialises in aerospace medicine, biomechanics and life-support systems for defence applications, including pilot safety equipment.

 

NOTE

 

• Defence Electronics Research Laboratory (DLRL) (Option A), based in Hyderabad, works on electronic warfare systems, not life-support systems.

 

• Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE) (Option B), based in Agra, works on parachutes and aerial delivery systems.

 

• Defence Laboratory Jodhpur (DLJ) (Option C) works on desert-related defence problems such as camouflage and agriculture in arid regions, not aviation life-support systems.

question: What is the name of Google's largest campus in India, unveiled in February 2025, that marks a milestone in the ongoing seismic shift in technology?
solution_text:

• Google unveiled 'Ananta', its largest campus in India, in February 2025, located in Bengaluru, marking a milestone in the company's expanding presence and its role in the ongoing technological shift driven by AI (गूगल का सबसे बड़ा भारतीय परिसर — 'अनंत', बेंगलुरु, फरवरी 2025).

 

• The name 'Ananta' (meaning 'infinite' or 'endless' in Sanskrit) reflects the campus's scale and Google's long-term commitment to India as a key hub for its global technology and engineering operations.

 

• The campus is designed to house thousands of Google employees and support the company's growing investments in cloud computing, artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Google (part of Alphabet Inc.) has had a significant presence in India for years, with major offices in Bengaluru, Gurugram, Hyderabad and Mumbai.

 

• India is one of Google's largest markets by user base, and the company has made substantial investments in digital skilling, AI research and startup support in the country.

 

• Other major tech companies have also expanded their India campuses in recent years, reflecting India's growing importance as a global technology and innovation hub.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahakaya (Option A), Vishaal (Option B) and Kshitij (Option D) are plausible-sounding Sanskrit-style names, but Google's largest India campus unveiled in February 2025 is officially named Ananta.

question: Which of the following is the goal of the India AI Safety Institute set up in January 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ensuring safe and ethical AI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The India AI Safety Institute (AISI), set up in January 2025, was established with the primary goal of ensuring safe and ethical development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence (भारत AI सुरक्षा संस्थान — सुरक्षित एवं नैतिक AI सुनिश्चित करना).

 

• The institute is part of India's broader AI governance framework, working alongside the IndiaAI Mission to promote responsible AI innovation while managing risks such as bias, misuse, misinformation and safety concerns arising from advanced AI systems.

 

• Such AI Safety Institutes have been established by several countries (including the UK, US and others) as AI capabilities have rapidly advanced, reflecting a global push towards coordinated AI governance and risk mitigation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IndiaAI Mission, approved by the Union Cabinet, aims to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem in India, covering compute infrastructure, datasets, applications, skilling, startups and safety/governance.

 

• The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is the nodal ministry overseeing India's AI policy initiatives.

 

• Global concerns around AI safety include issues like deepfakes, algorithmic bias, job displacement and existential risk from advanced AI systems, all of which are areas such institutes typically address.

 

NOTE

 

• Promoting online gaming (Option A), Developing quantum computers (Option B) and Regulating social media ads (Option D) are unrelated to the core mandate of the India AI Safety Institute, which is focused specifically on AI safety and ethics.

question: Which of the following services have been integrated into the newly revamped Mission Vatsalya Portal launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in July 2025?
option_1: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana and Sakhi
option_4: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Childline 1098
solution_text:
The correct answer is TrackChild and Khoya-Paya Services.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched a newly revamped Mission Vatsalya Portal in July 2025, integrating the TrackChild and Khoya-Paya services into it (मिशन वात्सल्य पोर्टल — TrackChild एवं खोया-पाया सेवाएँ एकीकृत).

 

• TrackChild is a portal used to track missing and found children, linking various stakeholders like police, Childline, NGOs and Child Welfare Committees, while Khoya-Paya is a citizen-engagement platform for reporting and searching for missing/found children.

 

• Mission Vatsalya is the umbrella centrally sponsored scheme for child protection and child welfare services in India, aiming to ensure a continuum of care for children in difficult circumstances, from prevention to institutional/non-institutional care.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mission Vatsalya subsumed the erstwhile Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) and focuses on strengthening child protection structures at the national, state and district levels.

 

• Childline 1098 is India's 24-hour national emergency helpline for children in distress.

 

• Other key schemes of the Ministry of Women and Child Development include Mission Shakti (women's safety and empowerment), Poshan Abhiyaan (nutrition), and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.

 

NOTE

 

• Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana and Sakhi (Option A), Poshan Abhiyaan and Ujjawala Scheme (Option C) and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Childline 1098 (Option D) are all genuine government schemes, but the specific services integrated into the revamped Mission Vatsalya Portal in July 2025 were TrackChild and Khoya-Paya.

question: In June 2025, the Government of India launched which of the following new disaster management tech platforms?
option_1: Integrated Centre Room for Emergency Response
option_2: Integrated Common Response for Emergency Response
option_3: Indian Control Room for Emergency Response
option_4: Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response
solution_text:
The correct answer is Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In June 2025, the Government of India launched the 'Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response', a new disaster management technology platform, to strengthen coordinated emergency response across agencies (एकीकृत नियंत्रण कक्ष — आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया, जून 2025).

 

• Such integrated control room platforms typically bring together data and communication from multiple emergency services — police, fire, ambulance, disaster management authorities — onto a single dashboard, enabling faster, better-coordinated responses to disasters and emergencies.

 

• This initiative aligns with India's ongoing efforts to modernise disaster management infrastructure under agencies like the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), leveraging technology for early warning, rapid response and resource coordination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) was established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.

 

• Other major disaster/emergency-related technology initiatives in India include the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP)-based early warning systems and the 112 India emergency helpline.

 

• India also participates in disaster preparedness through bodies like the National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) and international frameworks like the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.

 

NOTE

 

• Integrated Centre Room for Emergency Response (Option A), Integrated Common Response for Emergency Response (Option B) and Indian Control Room for Emergency Response (Option C) are all similarly worded distractors; the officially launched platform's correct name is the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response.

question: Who among the following was appointed as a Whole-time Member (Life) at the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in March 2025?

• Swaminathan S Iyer was appointed as a Whole-time Member (Life) at the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in March 2025 (IRDAI — स्वामीनाथन एस अय्यर, पूर्णकालिक सदस्य (जीवन बीमा)).

 

• IRDAI is the statutory regulatory body overseeing India's insurance industry, and its Whole-time Members oversee specific functional areas — the 'Life' member specifically oversees matters relating to the life insurance sector.

 

• IRDAI was established under the IRDA Act, 1999, to protect the interests of policyholders and regulate, promote and ensure the orderly growth of the insurance industry in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• IRDAI is headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana.

 

• The regulator oversees both life insurance and general (non-life) insurance companies operating in India, including public sector insurers like LIC and numerous private players.

question: How much carbon sink does the Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan released in 2025 aim to create by 2030?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A).39 billion tonnes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan, released in 2025, aims to create an additional carbon sink as stated in the option, by 2030 (हरित भारत मिशन — 2030 तक कार्बन सिंक लक्ष्य).

 

• The Green India Mission is one of the eight missions under India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), focused on protecting, restoring and enhancing India's forest cover to increase carbon sequestration.

 

• This target supports India's broader climate commitment under its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) to the Paris Agreement, which includes creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent through additional forest and tree cover by 2030.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green India Mission was launched in 2014 and is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

 

• India's Forest Survey of India (FSI) publishes the biennial India State of Forest Report (ISFR), tracking changes in the country's forest and tree cover.

 

• India ratified the Paris Agreement in 2016 and has committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.

 

NOTE

 

• 4 billion tonnes (Option B), C).5 billion tonnes (Option C) and 1 billion tonnes (Option D) are other plausible-looking figures presented as distractors, but the officially stated target under the Revised GIM Plan matches Option A.

question: Which of the following female runners won the women's race in the Paris Marathon 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bedatu Hirpa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bedatu Hirpa, an Ethiopian long-distance runner, won the women's race at the Paris Marathon 2025 (पेरिस मैराथन 2025 — महिला वर्ग विजेता, बेदातु हिरपा).

 

• The Paris Marathon is one of the world's major annual marathon events, typically held in April, attracting elite runners from around the world, particularly strong fields from East African nations like Ethiopia and Kenya, which dominate world marathon running.

 

• Ethiopian and Kenyan runners have consistently dominated major world marathons in recent years, owing to a strong distance-running tradition and high-altitude training in their home regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major world marathons include the World Marathon Majors: Boston, London, Berlin, Chicago, New York City and Tokyo marathons — the Paris Marathon, while very prestigious, is a major European marathon outside this official six-race series.

 

• The current world record holders in the marathon (as widely reported) include athletes such as Kelvin Kiptum (men's, Kenya) and Tigst Assefa (women's, Ethiopia), reflecting the continued East African dominance of the event.

 

• Marathon running has a rich history dating back to the ancient Greek legend of Pheidippides, and the modern marathon distance of 42.195 km was standardised at the 1908 London Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Letesenbet Gidey (Option B), Angela Tanui (Option C) and Dera Dida (Option D) are all elite East African distance runners, but the winner of the women's race at the Paris Marathon 2025 was Bedatu Hirpa.

question: In July 2025, which investigative authority unearthed over ₹24 crore in unaccounted assets in Karnataka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka Lokayukta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2025, the Karnataka Lokayukta unearthed over ₹24 crore in unaccounted assets during raids/investigations in Karnataka (कर्नाटक लोकायुक्त — ₹24 करोड़ की बेहिसाब संपत्ति उजागर).

 

• The Lokayukta is an anti-corruption ombudsman institution set up at the state level in India to investigate allegations of corruption and maladministration against public officials and government servants.

 

• Karnataka's Lokayukta institution is one of the more active state anti-corruption bodies in India, regularly conducting raids ('disproportionate assets' cases) against public officials found to have wealth disproportionate to their known sources of income.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lokayukta system in India was inspired by the concept of the Ombudsman in Scandinavian countries, and Maharashtra was the first Indian state to establish a Lokayukta, in 1971-72.

 

• At the central level, the equivalent anti-corruption body is the Lokpal, established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

 

• Other key anti-corruption/investigative agencies in India include the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).

 

NOTE

 

• Central Bureau of Investigation (Option A) and Enforcement Directorate (Option D) are central agencies that also investigate corruption/financial crimes, but this specific ₹24 crore unaccounted-assets case in Karnataka was unearthed by the state Lokayukta.

 

• Income Tax Department (Option C) investigates tax evasion and undisclosed income, but is not the agency credited with this particular Karnataka case.

question: In 2025, which Union Minister inaugurated the Khelo India multipurpose hall in Kamle district, Arunachal Pradesh?
solution_text:

• Mansukh Mandaviya, the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, inaugurated the Khelo India multipurpose hall in Kamle district, Arunachal Pradesh, in 2025 (मानसुख मांडविया — खेलो इंडिया बहुउद्देश्यीय हॉल, कमले, अरुणाचल प्रदेश).

 

• Khelo India is the Government of India's flagship scheme to promote sports at the grassroots level across the country, providing infrastructure, training and competitive opportunities to young athletes, including in remote and border regions like Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Developing sports infrastructure in North-Eastern states like Arunachal Pradesh is part of the government's broader push to identify and nurture sporting talent from every corner of the country, including border and tribal areas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khelo India scheme also includes the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India University Games and the Khelo India Winter Games, held in different parts of the country.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh's capital is Itanagar, and the state shares international borders with China (Tibet), Myanmar and Bhutan.

 

• Other key sports schemes/programmes in India include Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and the National Sports Awards, which include the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

 

NOTE

 

• Dharmendra Pradhan (Option B) is the Union Minister for Education, Kiren Rijiju (Option C) is a senior Union Minister (and MP from Arunachal Pradesh) who has previously held the Sports portfolio, and Anurag Thakur (Option D) is a former Union Sports Minister — but the inauguration in question was carried out by Mansukh Mandaviya.

question: In June 2025, the Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025 was held in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Germany.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025 was held in June 2025 in Bonn, Germany (बॉन जलवायु परिवर्तन सम्मेलन 2025 — जर्मनी).

 

• Bonn regularly hosts intersessional UNFCCC climate meetings (the mid-year technical/negotiating sessions) because it is home to the UNFCCC Secretariat headquarters, making it a natural venue for these preparatory climate talks ahead of the annual Conference of the Parties (COP).

 

• These Bonn sessions serve as important preparatory meetings where negotiators work through technical and procedural issues ahead of the year-end COP summit, helping build consensus before the main conference.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The UNFCCC (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change) Secretariat has been headquartered in Bonn, Germany, since 1996.

 

• COP (Conference of the Parties) is the supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC, held annually in a different host country/city; recent COPs include COP28 (Dubai, UAE, 2023) and COP29 (Baku, Azerbaijan, 2024).

 

• The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015 at COP21 in Paris, is the landmark international treaty on climate change, aiming to limit global warming to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.

 

NOTE

 

• France (Option A) and Paris (Option C) are associated with the Paris Agreement (COP21, 2015), not the Bonn intersessional conference.

 

• Switzerland (Option B) hosts other major international bodies (like the WHO and WTO in Geneva) but was not the venue for the Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025.

question: As per Union Budget 2025–26, for how many years has the Cotton Mission been planned to enhance cotton productivity, especially in extra-long staple varieties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 years.

• As per the Union Budget 2025-26, the Cotton Mission (Mission for Cotton Productivity) has been planned for a period of 5 years to enhance cotton productivity, with special focus on extra-long staple (ELS) cotton varieties (कपास मिशन — 5 वर्षीय योजना, अतिरिक्त लंबे रेशे की किस्में).

 

• The mission aims to promote science and technology-driven interventions in cotton cultivation, supporting farmers with better seeds and practices, and increasing India's competitiveness in high-quality cotton production and textile exports.

 

• Extra-long staple (ELS) cotton is a premium quality cotton with longer fibre length, used to make finer, high-value textiles, and India has historically been a significant importer of ELS cotton — this mission aims to boost domestic production of such varieties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is one of the largest producers of cotton in the world, and cotton (along with jute) is often referred to as one of the important cash crops and fibre crops of India.

 

• The Union Budget 2025-26 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, and included various sector-specific missions to boost agricultural productivity, including this focus on cotton.

 

• Major cotton-growing states in India include Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

 

NOTE

 

• 12 years (Option A), 10 years (Option B) and 2 years (Option D) are all incorrect durations; the Cotton Mission announced in Budget 2025-26 was planned for a 5-year period.

question: Which Pakistani female cricketer was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in June 2025?
solution_text:

• Sana Mir, the former Pakistan women's cricket team captain, was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in June 2025 (सना मीर — पाकिस्तान महिला क्रिकेट, ICC हॉल ऑफ फेम 2025).

 

• Sana Mir was a highly successful off-spin bowler and long-serving captain of the Pakistan women's team, and was instrumental in raising the profile and competitiveness of women's cricket in Pakistan during her career.

 

• The ICC Hall of Fame honours legendary cricketers (both men and women) who have made an outstanding and lasting contribution to the sport, based on their playing careers and impact on the game.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ICC (International Cricket Council) Hall of Fame was established in 2009 and inducts new members periodically, recognising cricketing greats from across cricketing nations and eras.

 

• Notable Indian cricketers inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame include Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Anil Kumble and, among women, players like Jhulan Goswami.

 

• Pakistan has a proud cricketing history, having won the Cricket World Cup in 1992 under the captaincy of Imran Khan.

 

NOTE

 

• Bismah Maroof (Option A) is another prominent former Pakistan women's captain, Diana Baig (Option C) is a current Pakistani fast bowler/all-rounder, and Nida Dar (Option D) is a senior Pakistani all-rounder — but the ICC Hall of Fame inductee referred to here is Sana Mir.

question: Who joined as the Mission Director of Atal Innovation Mission under NITI Aayog in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deepak Bagla.

• Deepak Bagla joined as the Mission Director of the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) under NITI Aayog in 2025 (दीपक बागला — अटल इनोवेशन मिशन, नीति आयोग).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015, and serves as the government's premier policy think tank.

 

• Atal Tinkering Labs, set up under AIM in schools across India, provide students with tools and equipment to develop skills in STEM, innovation and design thinking.

 

• The Atal Innovation Mission is named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

Paul (Option A) is a Member of NITI Aayog handling the Health vertical, Poonam Gupta (Option B) is associated with economic research/RBI-linked roles, and B S Subrahmanyam (Option D) is the current CEO of NITI Aayog — but the Mission Director of the Atal Innovation Mission appointed in 2025 was Deepak Bagla.

question: Who was named the Men's Player of the Year at the AIFF Awards 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhasish Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subhasish Bose, an Indian footballer known for his role as a defender, was named the Men's Player of the Year at the AIFF (All India Football Federation) Awards 2025 (सुभाषीश बोस — AIFF पुरस्कार 2025, वर्ष का सर्वश्रेष्ठ पुरुष खिलाड़ी).

 

• The AIFF Awards are presented annually to recognise outstanding performances and contributions in Indian football, across categories like Men's/Women's Player of the Year, Emerging Player, and Goalkeeper of the Year.

 

• Subhasish Bose has been a key player for both his club sides in the Indian Super League (ISL) and the Indian national football team, valued for his versatility and consistency at the back.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) is the governing body for football in India, and organises national competitions including the Indian Super League (ISL) (jointly with other stakeholders) and the Santosh Trophy.

 

• The Indian national football team is nicknamed the 'Blue Tigers', and Sunil Chhetri is widely regarded as the most iconic Indian footballer of the modern era.

 

• India has hosted major football events including the FIFA U-17 World Cup in 2017.

 

NOTE

 

• Brison Fernandes (Option A), Vishal Kaith (Option C) and Khalid Jamil (Option D) are all notable figures in Indian football (players/coach), but the AIFF Men's Player of the Year for 2025 was Subhasish Bose.

question: How many indigenously developed weapon systems were released by Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO) in June 2024 to Indian armed forces under the emergency procurement clause?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In June 2024, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) released 28 indigenously developed weapon systems to the Indian armed forces under the emergency procurement clause (DRDO — 28 स्वदेशी हथियार प्रणालियाँ, आपातकालीन खरीद प्रावधान, जून 2024).

 

• The emergency procurement clause/powers allow the Indian armed forces to fast-track the acquisition of critical defence equipment, bypassing some of the lengthier standard procurement processes, in order to quickly address urgent operational requirements.

 

• This move reflects India's growing thrust on indigenisation of defence production ('Atmanirbhar Bharat' in defence), ensuring that home-grown weapon systems developed by DRDO are rapidly inducted into active service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation), headquartered in New Delhi, is India's primary agency for military research and development, working under the Ministry of Defence.

 

• India's defence indigenisation push includes initiatives like the Positive Indigenisation Lists, which bar the import of specified defence items beyond certain timelines, encouraging domestic manufacturing.

 

• Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) in defence aims to reduce India's historically high dependence on imported military hardware and boost the domestic defence industrial base, including public sector units and private manufacturers.

 

NOTE

 

• 18 (Option A), 38 (Option B) and 48 (Option C) are plausible-looking distractor figures, but the actual number of indigenously developed weapon systems released by DRDO under the emergency procurement clause in June 2024 was 28.

question: Where is the embryo implanted after fertilisation in the human female body under normal conditions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uterus lining.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After fertilisation, the developing embryo (blastocyst) travels down the fallopian tube and gets implanted in the lining of the uterus, called the endometrium (गर्भाशय की भित्ति — भ्रूण का रोपण). This process is called implantation.

 

• Implantation usually occurs about 6-7 days after fertilisation, once the endometrium has thickened under the influence of the hormones progesterone and oestrogen to receive and nourish the embryo.

 

• After implantation, the placenta develops, which connects the embryo to the mother's blood supply and enables exchange of nutrients, oxygen and waste products throughout pregnancy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fertilisation (fusion of sperm and egg) normally takes place in the fallopian tube (oviduct), specifically in its ampulla region, not in the uterus itself.

 

• The fertilised egg is called a zygote; it undergoes repeated cell division to form a blastocyst by the time it reaches the uterus.

 

• The normal duration of human pregnancy (gestation period) is about 280 days (40 weeks) from the last menstrual period.

 

NOTE

 

• Oviduct (Option A): The fallopian tube, the site of fertilisation, not implantation.

 

• Ovary (Option B): The organ that produces the egg (ovum); it is not the site of implantation.

 

• Cervix (Option D): The narrow lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina; it is not where the embryo implants.

question: The main thinking part of the human brain is located in the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fore-brain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fore-brain (prosencephalon) is the main thinking part of the human brain and includes the cerebrum, which controls thinking, memory, intelligence, voluntary actions and interpretation of sensory information (अग्रमस्तिष्क — सोचने-समझने का केंद्र).

 

• The cerebrum is divided into two cerebral hemispheres (left and right) connected by the corpus callosum, and its outer layer, the cerebral cortex, is highly folded to increase surface area for greater processing capacity.

 

• The fore-brain also includes the thalamus and hypothalamus, which relay sensory information and regulate body temperature, hunger and thirst respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The human brain has three main parts: fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain.

 

• The hind-brain consists of the cerebellum (balance and coordination), pons and medulla oblongata (controls involuntary actions like heartbeat, breathing and blood pressure).

 

• The brain is protected by three membranes called meninges and by a bony case called the cranium, and is cushioned by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

 

NOTE

 

• Spinal cord (Option A): Part of the central nervous system that carries messages between the brain and the body; it is not part of the brain.

 

• Mid-brain (Option C): A small part connecting the fore-brain and hind-brain; controls reflex movements of the eye and head.

 

• Medulla (Option D): Part of the hind-brain that controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat, breathing and blood pressure, not thinking.

question: Which of the following is a diatomic molecule formed by a non-metallic element?
solution_text:
The correct answer is O₂ (Oxygen).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• O₂ (oxygen gas) is a diatomic molecule made up of two atoms of the non-metallic element oxygen joined together (द्विपरमाणुक अणु — ऑक्सीजन गैस).

 

• A diatomic molecule is one that consists of exactly two atoms, which may be of the same element (homonuclear, like O₂, N₂, H₂) or of different elements (heteronuclear, like HCl, CO).

 

• Non-metals such as oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, chlorine and fluorine commonly exist as diatomic molecules in their elemental gaseous state because a single covalent bond (or multiple bond) between two atoms fully satisfies their valency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common diatomic gaseous elements to remember: H₂, N₂, O₂, F₂ and Cl₂ (and the liquid/solid halogens Br₂, I₂).

 

• Ozone (O₃), in contrast, is a triatomic allotrope of oxygen, made of three oxygen atoms.

 

• Noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, etc.) exist as single, isolated atoms (monatomic), because their outer shell is already complete and stable.

 

NOTE

 

• He (Option B): Helium is a noble gas and exists as a monatomic molecule, not diatomic.

 

• Mg (Option C): Magnesium is a metal and does not exist as a simple diatomic molecule; metallic solids have a giant metallic lattice structure.

 

• Na (Option D): Sodium is also a metal, existing in a metallic crystal lattice, not as discrete diatomic molecules.

question: What are the primary functions of xylem and phloem tissues in a plant?
option_1: Both xylem and phloem transport food.
option_2: Xylem transports water and minerals, phloem transports food.
option_3: Both xylem and phloem transport water and minerals.
option_4: Xylem transports food, phloem transports water and minerals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Xylem transports water and minerals, phloem transports food.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Xylem is a vascular tissue that transports water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots to the stem, leaves and other parts of the plant (जाइलम — जल एवं खनिज लवणों का परिवहन).

 

• Phloem is a vascular tissue that transports food (prepared by photosynthesis, mainly as sucrose) from the leaves to all other parts of the plant, including storage organs and roots — a process called translocation.

 

• Movement in xylem is essentially unidirectional (upward, driven mainly by transpiration pull), while movement in phloem can be bidirectional, depending on the plant's needs (source to sink).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Xylem is made up of tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma; xylem vessels and tracheids are dead cells with lignified walls.

 

• Phloem is made up of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma; sieve tube cells are living cells but lack a nucleus at maturity.

 

• Together, xylem and phloem make up the vascular bundle, which provides both transport and mechanical strength to the plant.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A and Option D are incorrect because they either assign both tissues the same function or swap the roles.

 

• Option C is incorrect because phloem transports food, not water and minerals.

question: Which of the following is the chemical formula of fullerene carbon allotropes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C60.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon in which carbon atoms are arranged in a closed, hollow, cage-like structure; the most common and stable fullerene has the formula C60, popularly called Buckminsterfullerene or a 'buckyball' (फुलरीन — C60, बकीबॉल).

 

• The C60 molecule is shaped like a football (soccer ball), made up of 20 hexagonal and 12 pentagonal rings, with a carbon atom at each vertex.

 

• Fullerene was the third allotrope of carbon to be discovered (after diamond and graphite) and, unlike diamond and graphite, exists as discrete molecules, not a continuous lattice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diamond: each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a rigid 3-D tetrahedral lattice, making it the hardest known natural substance and a poor conductor of electricity.

 

• Graphite: carbon atoms are arranged in flat hexagonal layers that can slide over each other, making it soft, slippery and a good conductor of electricity (used in pencils, lubricants and electrodes).

 

• Fullerenes were discovered in 1985 by Robert Curl, Harold Kroto and Richard Smalley, who were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1996 for this discovery.

 

NOTE

 

• Options B, C and D do not represent the correct/standard fullerene formula; C60 (and larger cage structures like C70) are the well-known fullerenes.

question: Which of the following methods of reproduction ensures rapid increase in population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asexual reproduction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asexual reproduction produces a large number of offspring rapidly because it involves only a single parent, requires no mate-finding or fertilisation, and offspring can themselves reproduce quickly, leading to an exponential rise in population (अलैंगिक जनन — तीव्र जनसंख्या वृद्धि).

 

• Organisms like bacteria, yeast, amoeba, hydra and many plants (through vegetative propagation) use asexual reproduction and can multiply their numbers very fast under favourable conditions — for example, bacteria can double their population in a matter of minutes by binary fission.

 

• Because offspring produced asexually are genetically identical (clones) to the parent, there is no time lost in genetic recombination, which further speeds up population growth compared with sexual reproduction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common methods of asexual reproduction: binary fission (amoeba, bacteria), budding (yeast, hydra), fragmentation (Spirogyra), spore formation (Rhizopus, fungi) and vegetative propagation (potato, ginger).

 

• Sexual reproduction, by contrast, involves fusion of male and female gametes and produces genetically varied offspring, which promotes diversity but is generally slower for population growth.

 

• Asexual reproduction produces offspring with no genetic variation, making the population more vulnerable to being wiped out entirely by a single unfavourable change (like a new disease).

 

NOTE

 

• Self pollination (Option B) and Cross pollination (Option C) are both types of sexual reproduction in plants (pollination is only the transfer of pollen, not the complete reproductive process).

 

• Internal fertilisation (Option D) is a mode of sexual reproduction found in many animals, where fusion of gametes occurs inside the female body; it does not by itself cause rapid population increase.

question: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with a speed of 3 m/s. Its kinetic energy is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 9 J.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion, given by the formula KE = ½mv², where m is mass (in kg) and v is velocity (in m/s) (गतिज ऊर्जा — KE = ½mv²).

 

• Substituting the given values: KE = ½ × 2 kg × (3 m/s)² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 Joules.

 

• Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity and its SI unit is the Joule (J), the same unit used for all forms of energy and work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration, e.g. gravitational PE = mgh.

 

• The work-energy theorem states that the work done on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy.

 

• Kinetic energy depends on the square of velocity, so doubling the speed of an object quadruples its kinetic energy (for the same mass).

 

NOTE

 

• 6 J (Option A): Would result from an incorrect calculation, e.g. omitting the square on velocity or the factor of ½ incorrectly.

 

• 3 J (Option C) and 18 J (Option D): Both result from arithmetic errors in applying the formula ½mv²; only 9 J is correct.

question: Which of the following organs is present in chest cavity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lungs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The lungs are located in the chest (thoracic) cavity, protected by the rib cage, and are the primary organs of the respiratory system where gaseous exchange takes place (फेफड़े — वक्ष गुहा में स्थित).

 

• The thoracic cavity also houses the heart (in the mediastinum, between the two lungs) and is separated from the abdominal cavity below by the diaphragm, a dome-shaped muscle important for breathing.

 

• The lungs are covered by a double-layered membrane called the pleura, and the space between the layers contains a small amount of fluid that reduces friction during breathing movements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The abdominal cavity, located below the diaphragm, houses organs such as the liver, stomach, pancreas, spleen, kidneys and intestines.

 

• The right lung has three lobes and the left lung has two lobes (smaller, to accommodate the heart).

 

• Breathing is brought about by movement of the diaphragm and the intercostal muscles, which change the volume of the thoracic cavity.

 

NOTE

 

• Liver (Option A): The largest gland in the body; located in the abdominal cavity, on the right side, below the diaphragm.

 

• Pharynx (Option B): Part of the throat, common passage for food and air; located in the neck/head region, not the chest cavity proper.

 

• Pancreas (Option C): A gland that lies in the abdominal cavity, behind the stomach, and secretes both digestive enzymes and hormones like insulin.

question: The speed of sound in air is approximately 340 m/s. If a reflecting surface is 17 m away, how long does it take for an echo to return to the source?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.1 s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An echo is heard when a sound wave reflects off a surface and returns to the source; the sound must travel to the surface and back, so the total distance covered is twice the distance to the reflecting surface (प्रतिध्वनि — ध्वनि का परावर्तन).

 

• Total distance travelled by sound = 2 × 17 m = 34 m.

 

• Time taken = distance ÷ speed = 34 m ÷ 340 m/s = 0.1 second.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• For an echo to be distinctly heard by the human ear, the reflected sound must reach the listener at least 0.1 second after the original sound, because the sensation of sound persists in our ear for about that duration.

 

• This means the minimum distance of a reflecting surface for an echo to be heard is about 17.2 m (using speed of sound ≈ 344 m/s), matching the value given in this question.

 

• The speed of sound in air depends on temperature and is generally taken as about 340-346 m/s at room temperature; it is faster in liquids and fastest in solids.

 

NOTE

 

• A).05 s (Option A): Would result from forgetting to double the distance (using 17 m instead of 34 m) — this is half the minimum time needed for a perceptible echo.

 

• B).5 s (Option B) and 1 s (Option C): Both are larger than the correctly calculated value and do not match the given data of 340 m/s and 17 m.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about acceleration due to gravity?
option_2: It increases as we go inside the Earth
option_4: It is the same everywhere on Earth
solution_text:
The correct answer is It decreases with altitude.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The acceleration due to gravity (g) decreases as altitude (height above the Earth's surface) increases, because g is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the Earth's centre: g = GM/R² (गुरुत्वीय त्वरण — ऊँचाई बढ़ने पर घटता है).

 

• As you move away from the Earth's surface, the effective value of R (distance from the centre) increases, so g decreases; at a very large height, g approaches zero.

 

• Similarly, g also decreases with depth below the Earth's surface (as you go towards the centre), becoming zero at the centre of the Earth — it is not constant with depth, as claimed in one of the other options.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The value of g is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator, because the Earth is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator (making the polar radius smaller).

 

• The average value of g on the Earth's surface is taken as 9.8 m/s² (sometimes approximated as 10 m/s² or 9.81 m/s²).

 

• Weight (W = mg) of an object therefore varies with location, while its mass remains constant everywhere.

 

NOTE

 

• It increases as we go inside the Earth (Option B): Incorrect — g actually decreases as we go towards the Earth's centre.

 

• It remains constant with depth (Option C): Incorrect — g varies with depth, becoming zero at the centre.

 

• It is the same everywhere on Earth (Option D): Incorrect — g varies slightly with latitude and altitude due to the Earth's shape and rotation.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a tissue of an organism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neuron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A neuron (nerve cell) is a single cell — the structural and functional unit of the nervous system — not a tissue in itself; the tissue made up of neurons is called nervous tissue (न्यूरॉन — तंत्रिका कोशिका, ऊतक नहीं).

 

• A tissue is defined as a group of similar cells (along with intercellular substance) that work together to perform a specific function; Bone, Blood and Muscle are all recognised types of tissue, each made up of many cells of a similar kind.

 

• Bone and Blood are both types of connective tissue, while Muscle is one of the four fundamental animal tissue types (the others being epithelial, connective and nervous tissue).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four basic types of animal tissue are: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular and Nervous tissue.

 

• Blood is a fluid connective tissue, consisting of plasma along with red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

 

• Bone is a hard, rigid connective tissue that provides the skeletal framework and support for the body.

 

NOTE
