• Always verify the derived rule against BOTH given examples before applying it — a rule matching only one example could be a coincidence.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only two people sit between F and B when counted from the right of F. Only two people sit between B and A when counted from the right of B. Only three people sit between F and E when counted from the right of F. D sits to the immediate left of C. How many people sit between F and G when counted from the left of F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• A, B, C, D, E, F, G sit around a circular table facing the centre. Only two sit between F and B (counted from F's right); only two between B and A (from B's right); only three between F and E (from F's right); D is immediately left of C.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two between F and B, from the right of F' places B three seats clockwise (to the right) of F.

 

• 'Only two between B and A, from the right of B' places A three seats further along from B — working out, A ends up one seat anticlockwise (left) of F.

 

• 'Only three between F and E, from the right of F' places E four seats clockwise of F.

 

• With F, B, A and E fixed on the 7-seat circle, only three seats remain for C, D and G; 'D immediately left of C' fits only one of the remaining consecutive seat pairs, fixing D and C, and leaving G in the last seat.

 

• Counting from the left of F to G in this final arrangement, only one person (A) sits between them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular 'counted from the right/left of X' clues, first convert each clue into a fixed seat-gap (e.g. 'two between, from the right' = 3 seats clockwise) before trying to build the whole picture at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep 'left' and 'right' consistent throughout — they are defined from the perspective of the person mentioned in each specific clue, facing the centre of the table.

question: In a certain code language, 'queen area add' is coded as ' mk ng uk' and 'game queen ant' is coded as 'ng oz ie'. How is 'queen' coded in the given language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ng.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'queen area add' is coded as 'mk ng uk'; 'game queen ant' is coded as 'ng oz ie'. Find the code for 'queen'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word 'queen' is common to both given statements: it appears in 'queen area add' and in 'game queen ant'.

 

• The code word common to both coded outputs 'mk ng uk' and 'ng oz ie' is 'ng' — it is the only code-word present in both.

 

• Since 'queen' is the only word common to both statements, and 'ng' is the only code common to both codes, 'queen' must be coded as 'ng'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In such coded-language questions, find the word that repeats across two statements and match it to the code-word that repeats across their two coded forms — the matching pair gives you the answer directly, without needing to decode every word.

 

NOTE

 

• Never assume codes are given in the same left-to-right order as the words — always match by what is COMMON across two statements, as done here.

question:
Refer to the given number, symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

 

(Left) $ 9 $ 6 7 8 £ 5 1 8 2 £ 9 3 4 6 9 # 8 8 7 7 (Right)

 

How many such numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: (Left) $ 9 $ 6 7 8 £ 5 1 8 2 £ 9 3 4 6 9 # 8 8 7 7 (Right). Counting left to right.

 

SOLUTION

 

• We need numbers that are immediately preceded by a symbol (from $, £, #) AND immediately followed by a symbol.

 

• Scanning the sequence position by position, only the number 9 appearing right after the first '$' (and immediately before the second '$') satisfies both conditions — it is sandwiched between two symbols.

 

• No other number in the sequence has a symbol on both its immediate left and immediate right.

 

• Total count = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark every symbol in the sequence first; then check only the numbers that sit immediately next to a marked symbol on ONE side, and verify if a symbol also sits on the OTHER side.

 

NOTE

 

• Treat $, £ and # simply as 'a symbol' — the specific type of symbol does not matter for this condition, only that it IS a symbol.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

 

Statements:

Some teachers are writers.

All writers are professionals.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some professionals are teachers.

(II) All teachers are professionals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: Some teachers are writers. All writers are professionals.

 

• Conclusions: (I) Some professionals are teachers. (II) All teachers are professionals.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Some teachers are writers' means the teacher and writer groups overlap. 'All writers are professionals' means the entire writer group lies inside the professional group.

 

• So the overlapping part of teachers and writers also lies inside professionals, meaning teachers and professionals must overlap: this gives Conclusion (I), 'Some professionals are teachers' — this follows.

 

• Conclusion (II), 'All teachers are professionals', would require EVERY teacher to be a writer (and hence a professional), but the statement only says SOME teachers are writers — the remaining teachers' status is unknown. So (II) does NOT follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C — Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Some A are B' + 'All B are C' always gives 'Some A are C' (and its converse 'Some C are A') as a valid conclusion — but never gives 'All A are C'.

 

NOTE

 

• A conclusion using 'All' can follow only from premises that are themselves both universal ('All...are...') — a 'Some' premise anywhere in the chain blocks any 'All' conclusion.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the sister of B',

A − B means 'A is the mother of B',

A × B means 'A is the husband of B' and

A ÷ B means 'A is the brother of B'.

 

Based on the above, how is T related to J if 'T + K ÷ S × U - J'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Father's sister.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: A + B = A is sister of B; A − B = A is mother of B; A × B = A is husband of B; A ÷ B = A is brother of B.

 

• Expression: T + K ÷ S × U − J.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Break the expression into its linked relations, symbol by symbol: T + K → T is sister of K. K ÷ S → K is brother of S. S × U → S is husband of U. U − J → U is mother of J.

 

• Since U is J's mother and S is U's husband, S is J's father.

 

• K is brother of S, and T is sister of K — so T, K and S are all siblings of one another, making T the sister of S (since T is female and shares the same siblings as S).

 

• Since S is J's father and T is S's sister, T is J's father's sister, i.e. J's paternal aunt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Decode the expression one symbol at a time from left to right, writing out each relation in plain words, and only THEN connect the chain to answer the final relationship — trying to solve it in your head all at once invites mistakes.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch the gender implied by each code: '+' and '−' name a female relation (sister/mother), while '×' and '÷' name a male relation (husband/brother) — use this to keep track of who is male and who is female through the chain.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

 

UXZ 79, QTV 77, MPR 75, ILN 73, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. EHJ 71.

 

GIVEN

question: Which of the following labs under the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), successfully conducted high-altitude trials of the Indigenous On-Board Oxygen Generating System (OBOGS)-based Integrated Life Support System (ILSS) for the LCA Tejas aircraft, on March 04, 2025?

NOTE

• Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE) (Option B), based in Agra, works on parachutes and aerial delivery systems.

question: In July 2025, which investigative authority unearthed over ₹24 crore in unaccounted assets in Karnataka?

question: How many indigenously developed weapon systems were released by Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO) in June 2024 to Indian armed forces under the emergency procurement clause?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28.

• In June 2024, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) released 28 indigenously developed weapon systems to the Indian armed forces under the emergency procurement clause (DRDO — 28 स्वदेशी हथियार प्रणालियाँ, आपातकालीन खरीद प्रावधान, जून 2024).

 

• The emergency procurement clause/powers allow the Indian armed forces to fast-track the acquisition of critical defence equipment, bypassing some of the lengthier standard procurement processes, in order to quickly address urgent operational requirements.

 

• This move reflects India's growing thrust on indigenisation of defence production ('Atmanirbhar Bharat' in defence), ensuring that home-grown weapon systems developed by DRDO are rapidly inducted into active service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation), headquartered in New Delhi, is India's primary agency for military research and development, working under the Ministry of Defence.

 

• India's defence indigenisation push includes initiatives like the Positive Indigenisation Lists, which bar the import of specified defence items beyond certain timelines, encouraging domestic manufacturing.

 

• Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) in defence aims to reduce India's historically high dependence on imported military hardware and boost the domestic defence industrial base, including public sector units and private manufacturers.

 

NOTE

 

• 18 (Option A), 38 (Option B) and 48 (Option C) are plausible-looking distractor figures, but the actual number of indigenously developed weapon systems released by DRDO under the emergency procurement clause in June 2024 was 28.
